# Damaged-member fixtures

Each archive holds the text members `a.txt`, `b.txt` and `c.txt` (6000 bytes each; the
two-folder 7z adds `d.txt`), and only the data of `b.txt` is damaged; the headers and the
listing are intact. They are regenerated by:

```bash
uv run python scripts/fixtures/gen_damaged_member_fixtures.py
```

The script needs `7z`, RARLAB `rar` and `unrar`. Before it writes a fixture it checks the
damage with `7z t` or `unrar t`, which must fail exactly the members in the last column.
They are committed so the test runs where `rar` is absent (ADR
[0016](../../../dev-docs/decisions/0016-committed-rar-corpus-fixtures.md)), and the 7z ones
with them so the set is built one way.

| File | Written with | Damage | Tester fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `7z_copy_nonsolid.7z` | `7z a -mx0 -ms=off` | one byte inside `b.txt`: CRC mismatch | `b.txt` |
| `7z_lzma_nonsolid.7z` | `7z a -mx5 -ms=off` | 16 bytes in `b.txt`'s folder | `b.txt` |
| `7z_lzma_solid.7z` | `7z a -mx5 -ms=on`, one folder | 16 bytes in the folder, inside `b.txt` | `b.txt`, `c.txt` |
| `7z_lzma_2folders.7z` | `7z a -mx5 -ms=2f`, folders (`a`, `b`) and (`c`, `d`) | 16 bytes in the first folder, inside `b.txt` | `b.txt` |
| `rar5_stored.rar` | `rar a -m0 -ma5` | one byte inside `b.txt`: CRC mismatch | `b.txt` |
| `rar5_nonsolid.rar` | `rar a -m3 -ma5` | 16 bytes in `b.txt`'s data | `b.txt` |
| `rar5_solid.rar` | `rar a -m3 -ma5 -s` | 16 bytes in the solid stream, inside `b.txt` | `b.txt`, `c.txt` |

Used by `tests/test_damaged_member_pass.py`, which also builds the ZIP, TAR and ISO cases
itself.
